chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from al-Husayn ibn Rashid ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan or Abu Ja'far (peace be upon them) say regarding this verse: 'And they do not disobey you in what is known' (Ma'ruf). He said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Fatimah (peace be upon her): 'When I die, do not scratch your face, do not let down your hair, do not call out wailing, and do not employ a professional mourner for me.'
Then he said: This is the 'Ma'ruf' (what is known/customary) about which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said in His Book: 'And they do not disobey you in what is known'.

key_terms.الْوَيْل: Al-Wail (wailing/crying out), a specific form of loud, expressive mourning.
key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: Saww (peace be upon him and his family), an honorific used for the Prophet Muhammad.
key_terms.مَعْرُوف: Ma'ruf (that which is known/customary/good), referring to established social and religious etiquette.
key_terms.نَائِحَة: Na'ihah (professional female mourner), one who wails loudly and professionally over the dead.

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'in what is known' (fi ma'ruf) refer to in the context of the Prophet's instruction to Fatimah?
ai.summary: In this exegetical narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (or al-Baqir) interprets 'Ma'ruf' in Surah At-Tahrim as the specific, customary etiquette of mourning prescribed by the Prophet to Fatimah (peace be upon her). This interpretation highlights the continuity between prophetic instruction and divine command, emphasizing that adherence to the Prophet's specific guidance regarding modest grief—such as refraining from excessive wailing or professional mourners—is an act of obedience to God. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Prophet's Sunnah serves as a practical manifestation of Quranic principles.

en.basel-kadem: 32.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan al-Saffar, from Ya’qoub bin Yazid, from Hammad bin Isa, from Huraiz bin Abdullah, from Zurara, that he said: Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, said: Beware from wrapping in the manner of ssammaa’. He said: I said: And what is ssammaa’? That you make the cloth enter beneath your side, and so you place it on one shoulder.
